title: Designing Gmail

facts.text: When Alice composes an email in her Outlook client and presses send, the client sends it to the Outlook mail server, using SMTP between client and server.
The sender's mail server queries DNS to find the address of the recipient's SMTP server, which here is Gmail's.
It then transfers the email to the Gmail mail server, and the protocol between the two mail servers is also SMTP.
The Gmail server stores the email and makes it available to the recipient, Bob.
When Bob logs in to Gmail, the Gmail client fetches new emails through the IMAP/POP server.

notes: thin: the guide only walks through one email going from a sender's client to a recipient's mailbox (SMTP, DNS lookup, IMAP/POP fetch). It has no requirements, scale estimates, mailbox storage or data model, search, spam filtering, attachments, API or scaling discussion.
